message: Exploratory validation-only diagnostics (reports/exploratory/validation_diagnostics_v1.{yaml,md}; no protected data; no preregistered quantity changed), run at the researcher's request to ask whether the negative confirmatory results stem from our own design choices. D1: in every injected family the preregistered 10 s warning window before the first terminal event lies long after the injection has ended (median 24-105 s from injection end to window start; overlap 0 percent except localisation_perturbation 37.5 percent), so the task as labelled is predicting a delayed terminal consequence, not detecting the active fault; families with zero recall (lidar_dropout, wheel_slip, localisation_perturbation) show window maximum risk 0.06-0.10 versus 0.19-0.27 where detection works. D2: 200 hierarchical resamples of validation re-selecting the budgeted threshold give p05-p95 thresholds 0.128-0.314 around the frozen 0.235; resampled thresholds exceed the 0.10 clean-mission budget on the full validation set in 36 percent of replicates, and the frozen threshold exceeds the budget on 46 percent of resamples (p95 0.224), so the held-out false-alert rate 0.183 is within the selection's own sampling variance. D3: leave-one-validation-map-out selection shows no recall optimism on average (0.413 selection versus 0.478 left-out) but very large map-to-map spread (0.06, 0.75, 0.63 with 5-8 events per map). Interpretation for the manuscript: the confirmatory shortfall is consistent with (a) a label definition that places the warning window after the fault has ended, (b) a threshold budget estimated from 72 clean missions, and (c) few maps per split, rather than with an implementation defect; all three are our design choices and are reported as limitations, not as re-analysis.
